items.title: Exxon, Chevron warn fuel prices to endure as war knocks refining
items.summary: ExxonMobil and Chevron Corp. have warned that high fuel prices are likely to persist, even if crude oil prices fall, due to global refining capacity shortages caused by ongoing conflicts in Russia and the Middle East. Nearly 10% of the world's refining capability is offline, leading to record-high fuel-making margins for refiners but increased costs for consumers. This bottleneck is evident in rising gasoline and especially middle distillate prices, with little room for error in the highly utilized remaining refineries.

items.title: BATL, USO, UCO Edge Higher As Oil Gains: Exxon Executive Warns Shrinking Inventories Could Send Crude To $160
items.summary: ExxonMobil Senior Vice President Neil Chapman warned that global crude inventories are approaching unprecedented lows, which could drive Brent crude prices to $150-$160 per barrel. Chevron CEO Mike Wirth concurred, citing rapidly depleting strategic reserves amidst geopolitical tensions. Oil-related ETFs and major oil companies like Battalion Oil Corp. (BATL), United States Oil Fund (USO), and ProShares Ultra Bloomberg Crude Oil (UCO) saw gains in anticipation of higher prices.

items.title: Canadian National Railway raises its 2026 volume outlook as freight demand firms
items.summary: Canadian National Railway has increased its 2026 volume outlook, attributing the revision to stronger freight demand and successful second-quarter results with higher profit and revenue. This positive development, coupled with similar reports from Norfolk Southern, signals improving conditions for the freight and supply chain sectors, prompting shippers to re-evaluate rail capacity commitments. Additionally, DP World's new terminals in Fujairah offer a strategic bypass to the Strait of Hormuz, providing long-term benefits for Gulf-touching supply chains.

items.title: BrilliA Incorporated (NYSE American: BRIA) sees FY2026 profit dip, targets 2027 growth
items.summary: BrilliA Incorporated reported a dip in fiscal year 2026 profit with revenue falling to $49.0 million from $64.4 million due to U.S. tariff measures and order cancellations. Despite a small net loss of $15 thousand, the company remained profitable before income taxes and saw operating cash flow improve. BrilliA anticipates a return to growth in fiscal 2027, with preliminary first-quarter revenue up 13% year-on-year and second-quarter revenue expected to increase by approximately 30%.

items.title: Popular’s Earnings Beat Shows Why This Bank Stock Keeps Climbing
items.summary: Popular (NASDAQ: BPOP), Puerto Rico's largest bank, continues to demonstrate strong financial performance, leading to a "Buy" rating from analysts. The bank's second-quarter results showed significant earnings growth, increased dividends, and a new $1 billion stock buyback program, driven by robust net interest income and non-interest income. Despite potential concerns regarding rising credit costs and a leadership change, Popular's diversified banking footprint and strong capital levels position it well for continued growth, although its stock price is now trading near analyst targets, suggesting new investors may need to be more selective.

items.title: 5 Must-Read Analyst Questions From Sallie Mae’s Q2 Earnings Call
items.summary: Sallie Mae's Q2 performance missed analyst expectations for revenue and EPS due to increased noninterest expenses and a temporary dip in net interest margin. CEO Jonathan Witter noted stable credit quality despite the financial misses. Analysts focused on questions regarding net interest margin recovery, the impact of credit performance, loan yield normalization, back-half EPS guidance, and the decision to halt debt sales.

items.title: Down 31% this year, can Tesla stock bounce back?
items.summary: Tesla stock has fallen 31% this year, prompting questions about its recovery potential despite its strong long-term performance. The article suggests that increased competition from Chinese rivals and declining subsidies are squeezing Tesla's profit margins and free cash flow, making it an overpriced investment despite its past success. The author concludes that Tesla's current valuation of 287 times earnings does not reflect these challenges, advising against adding it to a portfolio.

items.title: Is Texas Capital Bancshares (TCBI) Undervalued After Its Buyback, Earnings, And Dividend Update?
items.summary: Texas Capital Bancshares (TCBI) has completed a US$98.19 million buyback program and announced fresh quarterly earnings and new dividend declarations. Despite a recent share price decline, the company shows positive long-term momentum and is considered undervalued by both analyst targets and intrinsic value estimates, specifically trading at a discount to a fair value narrative of $107.69 and an SWS DCF model estimate of $148.77. Investments in digital platforms and fee-based businesses are expected to drive efficiencies and resilient earnings, though concentration risk and operational demands from a recent data breach pose potential challenges.
